new_findings.text: RR:155 packs two different formulas into one sentence and gets the pairing backwards. In web v0.717 DAMAGE (§1t99s0§.as:3255-3271) light scales with light mastery (0.5 -> 0.9), balanced with balanced mastery (1.0 -> 1.2), and heavy is FLAT x1.4 with no mastery term at all - :3267-3270 fall through three cases to '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * 1.4;'. REACH (§1t99s0§.as:3091-3121) is the mirror image: light is FLAT x1.4 of base, balanced scales with balanced mastery (1.0 -> 1.2), and heavy scales with heavy mastery (0.5 -> 0.9) AND is clamped to a floor of 100 at :3117-3119. So exactly one of the three stances is mastery-flat in each table, and it is a different stance in each. The ledger's '(Heavy is fixed)' is true for damage only, and its 'Heavy's reach also scales x0.5 -> x0.9' is right but is the ONLY reach term it names.
new_findings.ledger_text: 3. **The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.** A level-1 Shugyosha does Light ×0.5 / Balanced ×1.0 / Heavy ×1.4 (Heavy is fixed); Heavy's *reach* also scales ×0.5→×0.9.
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters + L5 combat-core. Model two separate 3-entry tables with a mastery term on a DIFFERENT stance in each, plus a hard reach floor of 100 on heavy. The ledger's reach triple 300/200/100 is not reproducible from these multipliers at any single base.

new_findings.text: A false-negative trap of the same family as correction C1, for the string table this time. 'String N is absent from strings.json' does NOT imply 'N is a v0.717 addition'. Parsing the raw UTF-16LE XLIFF in reference/extracted/android/118_Mobile_Lang_EN.bin yields 2555 trans-unit ids, and in the range 850-1010 they run 850..865, 867..880, then jump straight to 1000. The whole block 881-999 is missing from the android v0.682 table - 119 consecutive ids, not one. So string 960's absence is a block gap, and any claim that infers 'web-only addition' from a single absent id in that range is resting on a hole, not on evidence. There are 20 such gaps in the table (largest: 1044->2000).
